qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Southeast US regional branch density and core retail/commercial deposit relationships create modest switching barriers. However, empirical capital efficiency fails the Munger hurdle: 10-year median ROIC is ~4.6-8.2% (FY25 ROIC ~6.4%, ROE ~8.2%), well below the 12% threshold. Commoditized loan pricing, rising deposit beta competition from money-center banks and fintechs, and the divestiture of its high-margin insurance brokerage (TIH) leave an undifferentiated spread-lending business lacking pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Truist operates a regional commercial banking franchise with sticky Southeast deposit density, but exhibits sub-hurdle capital efficiency with 10-year median ROIC of ~4.6-8.2% and ROE ~8%, far below the 12% compounder threshold. Prolonged integration friction following the BB&T/SunTrust merger and the subsequent divestiture of Truist Insurance Holdings (TIH) leave a commoditized spread-lending institution lacking structural pricing power against national money-center banks and private credit.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC is 4.6-8.2% (FY21: 7.2%, FY22: 6.3%, FY23: -0.78%, FY24: -0.73%, FY25: 6.42%), consistently failing the 12% hurdle across full credit cycles. Return on Equity (ROE) hovers around 7.6-8.4% with ROA at 0.90-1.00% on ~$540B in total assets. The 2019 merger of BB&T and SunTrust produced multi-year IT integration headwinds, elevated efficiency ratios, and customer friction. In 2024, Truist divested its highest-return, capital-light subsidiary (Truist Insurance Holdings) to Stone Point and CD&R to bolster regulatory capital and fund share buybacks. As a fractional-reserve commercial deposit bank, it faces high deposit betas, commoditized asset yields, and inherent credit and duration risks (g6_default: N).
